parts:
Hi Karl,
Doing single marker analysis I have the most significant marker associate with the trait in each chromosome. Is there any way to have all significant markers or the significant markers around the most significant one.

Thank you in advance for your help

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re:
parts:
I can't think of a simple way to do this.

You can use lodint() or bayesint() with expandtomarkers=TRUE to get a QTL interval; expandtomarkers=TRUE forces the end points to be at typed genetic markers.

    data(hyper)
    hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
    out <- scanone(hyper, method="em")
    lodint(out, chr=4, expandtomarkers=TRUE)
    bayesint(out, chr=4, expandtomarkers=TRUE)

If you want to find all of the markers in the region of a QTL, you might convert the genetic map to a data frame, find the marker at the QTL position, and then show the surrounding markers.

    maxpos <- max(out)
    marker <- find.marker(hyper, maxpos$chr, maxpos$pos)
    map <- pull.map(hyper)
    map_df <- map2table(map)
    row_index <- which(rownames(map_df) == marker)
    map_df[row_index + (-3:3), ]

karl
